# S-029 网络可行性评估 / Network Feasibility

**Source:** `artifacts/network_feasibility.json` (generated by `code/s029_10_network.py`),
`artifacts/quality_metrics.json`, `data/network_edges.jsonl`.
**Gate is evaluated before any structural number is interpreted.**

---

## 1. The quality gate (declared in advance, applied mechanically)

| gate | value | threshold | result |
|---|---:|---|---|
| G1 claims with a stable external id on ≥1 side | **100.0%** | ≥60% | pass |
| G2 claims resting on fuzzy/undated identity | **10.08%** | ≤15% | pass |
| G3 anachronism-flagged claims | **1.37%** | ≤5% | pass |
| G4 companies with ≥20 authoritative claims | **5 / 5** | ≥3 | pass |

**Gate passed → the structural inventory below is reported as interpretable description.** This is
deliberately narrower than "usable for prediction": the gate certifies that the relation layer is
traceable enough to *describe*, while the pre-registered conditions T3, T4 and T6 (institution identity, point-in-time
evidence and human adjudication) are what forbid a *time-ordered prediction experiment*.

## 2. Inventory

| quantity | value |
|---|---:|
| authoritative claims | 20,563 |
| unique deduplicated edges (subject, predicate, object) | **15,796** |
| entities | 7,059 |
| entities with a verified stable identifier | 5,220 |
| edges by predicate | `HAS_TOPIC` 7,455 · `SPONSORS_TRIAL` 4,209 · `AFFILIATED_WITH` 2,175 · `CO_AFFILIATED_ON` 1,225 · `HOSTS_TRIAL_SITE` 598 · `FUNDED_BY` 105 · `REFERENCES_PUBLICATION` 26 · `RESPONSIBLE_FOR_TRIAL` 3 |

The edge count is dominated by two things that are **not** company networks: MeSH topic assignment and
trial registration. Of 15,796 edges the organisation↔organisation subset is only `CO_AFFILIATED_ON`
(1,225) plus the trial-participation families; `AFFILIATED_WITH` (2,175), `HAS_TOPIC` (7,455) and
`REFERENCES_PUBLICATION` (26) also involve a publication, and only 105 involve declared funding. **A reader who equates "15,796 edges"
with "15,796 relationships between organisations" has been misled by the count.** The
organisation↔organisation part of this graph is small (see §3) and is either co-authorship or trial
participation, never confirmed cooperation.

## 3. Structure — reported as description, not as a property of the world

**Company ↔ institution co-affiliation graph:** 1,225 edges, **a single connected component of 1,056
nodes**. Company degree: Medtronic 382, Philips 302, GE HealthCare 287, Mindray 190, Dräger 64 (median
287). The giant component is an expected artefact of publication co-authorship: a paper by a
company-employed author and any hospital creates an edge, and hospitals publish repeatedly. It is not
evidence of a cohesive research community, and no centrality or community result is computed from it.

**Company ↔ trial graph:** 4,209 sponsor/collaborator edges. Company degree: Medtronic 1,667,
Philips 381, GE HealthCare 345, Dräger 18, Mindray 7. The **238×** spread between Medtronic and Mindray is a
**registry-naming and company-size** effect (Medtronic registers under dozens of unit names), not a
measurement of research intensity.

**Institution ↔ trial graph:** 598 site edges plus institution sponsors; sites are reported only for the
209-study sub-sample, so the site layer is a sample, not a census.

## 4. Sensitivity: what a canonical-name study would have seen

| measure | value |
|---|---:|
| records carrying a company mention | 3,134 |
| records reachable by the exact parent name only | 1,013 |
| **share lost if only the parent name were queried** | **67.68%** |

This is the most decision-relevant structural number in the study. Two-thirds of the evidence exists
under operating-unit, subsidiary or former-company strings. A network built from exact parent names
alone would be a different graph, not a smaller one — what it drops is concentrated in the companies
with the most internal divisional structure (Philips 99.5% of sponsor strings are units; Medtronic
61.8%), so the dropped part is systematically *not random*.

## 5. What is deliberately not computed, and why

| not computed | reason |
|---|---|
| centrality, PageRank, community detection | ranks would be driven by how many papers list an institution — an artefact measured in §D of the quality report (54.96% of claims rest on text affiliation) |
| temporal edge growth / burst detection | requires knowing what was knowable at a past date; **0 claims** have genuine observed-as-of evidence (§C.2) and the affiliation channel has a mechanical 2014 break (§C.4) |
| link prediction, GNN training | explicitly out of scope this round; also forbidden by the verdict |
| knowledge-flow direction | no collected record states a direction |
| "collaboration network" of any kind | Relation C has **zero** admissible rows; co-affiliation is not collaboration |

## 6. Verdict on network feasibility

The descriptive layer is feasible and now exists. The **temporal** layer that a prediction experiment
would need does not exist in this data: no relation is observed as-of, `valid_to` is empty everywhere,
and the only high-volume affiliation channel changes its own retrievability in 2014 by construction.

Therefore S-029's answer to RQ4 is:

> **`NO-GO FOR PREDICTION`** — the relations are reconstructable and individually traceable, but they are
> not point-in-time evidence and they are not human-validated. The next round must either acquire
> genuine observed-as-of history (a live collection that runs forward) or complete the human
> adjudication, before any temporal prediction is attempted. See `PHASE_REPORT_ZH.md` §6.
